robot.engineering_reasoning: The chassis provides a stable base for mounting components. Four cylindrical wheels are placed at symmetric ±Z positions for left/right separation and positive Y for ground contact, each rotated 90° about X to align rotation axis with Y (hinge axis [0,1,0]) for proper drive motion. The range sensor and camera are mounted front-center at elevated Y to maximize forward field of view. Compute, power, and controller units are stacked vertically along Y above the chassis to lower center of mass and protect from ground effects. All wheel joints are continuous hinges to allow unrestricted rotation for drive. Sensor and compute placements assume unimplemented perception and navigation stacks; no SLAM, mapping, or obstacle avoidance logic is included. Design adheres to Y-up coordinate convention with Z as lateral axis.
